message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Node CI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          cache: "yarn"
      - run: yarn install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: yarn lint

  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 5

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        node-version: [20.x, 22.x, 24.x]

    env:
      ENABLE_COVERAGE: true
      AST_COMPARE: true

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: "yarn"
      - run: yarn upgrade jest-light-runner@0.7.13
        if: ${{ matrix.node-version == '20.x'}}
      - run: yarn --frozen-lockfile
        if: ${{ matrix.node-version != '20.x'}}
      - run: yarn c8 yarn test:node
      - uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          fail_ci_if_error: true
          disable_search: true
          files: coverage/lcov.info
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
      - run: yarn test:standalone",
  "rationale": "The workflow has no per-job timeout, so a hung or very slow job can consume unbounded runner time. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by the catalogue pattern and by the measured fork experiment for the same pattern, which preserved all checks while reducing elapsed time. Adding a 5-minute per-job timeout bounds runaway consumption without removing any step, matrix cell (3 OS x 3 Node), required check, permission, or concurrency behavior, and without adding secrets, network access, or privileged actions. The observed successful runs complete in well under the proposed budget (about 90-136 s per workflow run, with lint and test running in parallel), giving headroom for cold installs and slower matrix cells while still catching genuinely stuck jobs.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT"]
}
